q: How many questions do you need for a 2-hour trivia night?
a: About 40-50 questions — typically 4 to 5 rounds of 8-10 questions each, plus a tiebreaker. Half of a live show's clock goes to reading, teams conferring, and scoring, so a 2-hour slot lands near 45 questions, not 90.

q: How many rounds should a trivia night have?
a: Four to five rounds for a standard 2-hour night, at 8-10 questions per round. Rounds create natural scoring breaks, let you vary the theme, and give the room a breather — which is why they matter more than the raw question count.

q: How long does each trivia question take?
a: Roughly 2 minutes of real time once you include reading it (often twice), teams writing their answer, and the back-and-forth. That rule of thumb is the fastest way to size a set to your available time.

q: How many questions for a 1-hour trivia night?
a: About 20-25 questions — 3 rounds of 7-8, or 2 rounds of 10 with a short break. Fewer, well-paced questions almost always play better than a packed sheet you have to rush through.
